name: GT-kitaev-operator-space-axioms
source: refs/kitaev-2405.02434/approximate_algebras.tex:1454-1463 VERBATIM: "A complex vector space $\calL$ is called an \emph{operator space} if each space $\Ma{n}\otimes\calL$ (for $n=1,2,\ldots$) is equipped with a norm $\|\cdot\|_n$ satisfying the following axioms: \begin{alignat}{2} \label{ax_R1} \|AXB\|_n &\le\|A\|\ts\|X\|_k\ts\|B\|\qquad & &(A\in\Ma{n,k},\quad B\in\Ma{k,n},\quad X\in\Ma{k}\otimes\calL),\\[3pt] \label{ax_R2} \left\|\begin{pmatrix}X&0\\ 0&Y\end{pmatrix}\right\|_{k+n} &=\max\bigl\{\|X\|_k,\|Y\|_n\bigr\}\qquad & & (X\in\Ma{k}\otimes\calL,\quad Y\in\Ma{n}\otimes\calL). \end{alignat} The norm on $\calL$ itself is defined by identifying $\calL$ with $\Ma{1}\otimes\calL$. An operator space is called \emph{self-adjoint} if it is equipped with a conjugate linear involution $\dagger$ that preserves all norms $\|\cdot\|_n$."
